title: Documenting Architecture Decisions
takes: A decision as a short record: its context, the decision, its consequences, and its status - proposed, accepted, superseded by another.

title: A Leader's Guide to After-Action Reviews (TC 25-20)
takes: Four questions after any action: what was planned, what happened, why, and what to do next time.

title: Agile Retrospectives: Making Good Teams Great
takes: A team looks back at the end of an iteration, at a set time - a ceremony of the iteration.

title: ast-grep: structural search and rewrite
takes: Code found and rewritten by its structure, written as code; formatting no longer matters. It cannot see inside Rust macros - their insides are tokens.

title: Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure (Site Reliability Engineering, ch. 15)
by: John Lunney and Sue Lueder, Google
takes: After a failure, a written, blameless account of what happened and what changes.

title: Psychophysical bases of perceived exertion
takes: A 0-10 category-ratio scale of perceived exertion: one number for how draining something was. The ledger's load.

title: Changesets
takes: Record the intent of a change when it is made, as a file beside it; a release consumes them, takes the highest bump, writes the changelog.

title: CHAOSS: Community Health Analytics in Open Source Software
takes: Metrics and tools (GrimoireLab, Augur) that measure open source projects' activity and health from the outside: commits, issues, reviews, mailing lists.

title: The Thing (the fence)
takes: Do not remove a fence until you know why it was put up: find out why something is as it is before changing it.

title: Wikipedia: Citation needed
takes: A need marked exactly where it is, in the thing itself, so that whoever passes can fill it.

title: Comby: structural code search and replace
takes: Structural rewriting by balanced delimiters, language-agnostic; another way, weighed and not taken.

title: Domain-Driven Design (the ubiquitous language)
takes: One language, used the same way in conversation, in code and in documents; a word that means two things is a bug.

title: Fulldome
takes: Immersive projection filling a dome - a planetarium's whole sky around the viewer - used to show not only the stars but their stories, and navigated in real time in digital planetariums.

title: The Toyota Way (go and see)
takes: Go and see the real thing for yourself - the device's own record, not a theory about it.

title: git interpret-trailers
takes: Machine-readable key: value lines at the end of a commit message (Signed-off-by, Fixes).

title: githooks - hooks used by Git
takes: Local hooks (pre-commit, prepare-commit-msg, commit-msg) can be bypassed with --no-verify; core.hooksPath moves them.

title: About Projects
takes: Items kept once, with fields of one's own, and many views - table, board, roadmap - over the same items.

title: Toyota Production System: Beyond Large-Scale Production
takes: Jidoka, automation with a human touch: the machine judges and stops itself on anything abnormal, so no person stands by to judge. Why tests must judge sound and pictures themselves.

title: Kanban: Successful Evolutionary Change for Your Technology Business
takes: Make the flow of work visible, limit work in progress, pull rather than push, make policies explicit, and measure how long work takes.

title: Knope
takes: Changesets and conventional commits in one Rust tool: the version and changelog picked from both.

title: Lens
takes: A lens is a transmissive device: it lets light through and, by bending it, brings it to a focus. It adds no light and displays nothing; what is seen forms where the light comes to focus.

title: The Linear Method
takes: Work as issues with an owner and a state; a small set of states; triage for what comes in; momentum over ceremony.

title: Development of NASA-TLX (Task Load Index)
by: Sandra G. Hart, Lowell E. Staveland
takes: Workload in six parts - mental, physical and time demand, performance, effort, frustration. Too heavy for every bump; kept in mind for a richer load later.

title: OPSLOG: introduction to log entries
takes: Each log entry has a key, a time and a type fixed when it is made, and points to the entry it relates to.

title: Obeya
takes: A big room (Toyota, the Prius project, Takeshi Uchiyamada, 1990s) whose walls show timing, milestones, progress and countermeasures to problems together, so that problems become visible; begun because no one person held the knowledge the work needed.

title: What I Saw When I Wasn't Sleeping: An Observing Log Primer
takes: An observer records notes at the eyepiece, while it is fresh; the log becomes the record of the journey, one object at a time.

title: The OODA loop
takes: Observe and orient before deciding and acting; the looking is part of the work, not a delay before it.

title: Politics and the English Language
takes: Prefer the short, everyday word; cut every word that can go; no jargon where an everyday word will do.

title: Governing the Commons: The Evolution of Institutions for Collective Action
takes: Commons last where those who use a resource can see its state and take part in its rules: clear boundaries, monitoring by the users themselves, collective choice, and enterprises nested within larger ones.

title: Federal Plain Language Guidelines
by: Plain Language Action and Information Network
takes: Write for the reader, in words they already know; one term for one thing, used the same way throughout.

title: The Principles of Product Development Flow
takes: Queues are the hidden cost of development; work that waits and ages is the signal to watch, more than how busy people are.

title: Ratatui
takes: Rust's terminal UI library, with a test backend that lets an interface be tested without a terminal.

title: release-please
takes: A release pull request kept from conventional commits: the version and a changelog of commit titles.

title: release-plz
takes: release-please's idea for Rust crates, with crates.io publishing.

title: The Reflective Practitioner: How Professionals Think in Action
takes: Practitioners learn by reflecting in action and on action: looking back is part of the work, not apart from it.

title: Shape Up, chapter 13: Show Progress (hill charts)
takes: Progress as uncertainty: uphill while still figuring it out, downhill once it is only doing.

title: Eliminating Toil (Site Reliability Engineering, chapter 5)
by: Vivek Rau; ed. Beyer, Jones, Petoff, Murphy
takes: Toil: manual, repetitive, automatable, tactical, without enduring value, growing with scale - counted and kept within a budget. The ledger counts exactly this.

title: Toyota Production System
takes: Jidoka and the andon: a problem is made visible the moment it happens, and the work stops for it rather than passing it on.

title: Tree-sitter
takes: An incremental parser behind ast-grep and many editors: the structure of code as a tree.

title: Is It Worth the Time?
takes: How much time an automation may cost before it pays: time per occurrence times frequency over a horizon.

title: Zooniverse: people-powered research
takes: Large work done by many through small, well-defined contributions that need no standing in the project.
